item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Redefining Agent Performance and Cost · 4 minute read

MiniMax M3.1 Flash delivers a generational leap in agentic tasks, coding, Computer Use, and cybersecurity. It makes online inference nearly three times faster and reduces usage costs by 70%. The model is now available through the MiniMax API, M Plan, and MiniMax Code. MiniMax plans to release the model weights at a later date.

Mercury 3 · 4 minute read

Inception Labs' Mercury 3 is a diffusion-based language model that reportedly outperformed GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on multiple benchmarks while generating over 1,000 tokens per second.

Introducing Clairic, a new System One class of extraction models · 16 minute read

Clairic can extract, compute, estimate, and forecast values from unstructured inputs. It is an 'extraction model', a new class of System One-style model that returns values directly extracted from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it. The model doesn't generate any tokens, so it can't produce a mistyped answer or hallucinate in the same way LLMs can. It can still make mistakes, but its outputs come with confidence scores to help users evaluate whether it is appropriate to trust the model or to take a second look.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Import AI 477: In which I tell the IMF the Singularity has begun · 22 minute read

AI's impact on national security and economic trajectories marks the onset of the singularity, accelerating scientific and technological progress. AI systems like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini are already solving complex problems in disciplines like mathematics, biology, and robotics, indicating potential for widespread innovation. To capitalize on these advancements, there needs to be significant infrastructure development and careful governance to navigate the associated risks and ensure equitable benefits.

AI Benchmarks: Climbing the Wrong Hills · 24 minute read

AI benchmarks are now shaping how models are evaluated in training and the capabilities they are designed to have. Poorly constructed benchmarks could push the industry in the wrong direction. Creating benchmarks impervious to benchmaxxing requires expertise in measuring what we actually want from AI systems. As benchmaxxing continues, researchers must decide which hills they want to climb and whether today's benchmarks actually reward progress in that direction.

Inside Meta's Gigawatt-Scale AI Supercluster · 14 minute read

Meta details the engineering behind Prometheus, its gigawatt-scale AI supercluster supporting the Muse model family. It explores its infrastructure design, plans to scale toward roughly one million GPUs, and closed-loop liquid cooling technology.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Introducing TorchNeuron: Native PyTorch backend for AWS Trainium · 27 minute read

TorchNeuron is an open-source native PyTorch backend for Trainium. It uses the model code, the libraries, and the tools developers already use on Trainium. TorchNeuron supports eager execution for research and debugging. It has been released in public Beta under the Apache 2.0 open source licence.

Introducing Exa 3.0 · 3 minute read

Exa 3.0 leads on evaluations spanning coding, finance, deep research, and company intelligence. The release includes Exa Lite, a new search type priced at $4 per 1,000 requests. Exa runs its own crawler and an independent index, tracking over 2 trillion URLs, serving 100 billion pages, and growing around what its customers search for. The index includes 1.27B ecommerce listings with prices and availability, over 211 million local businesses with hours and ratings, real-time news, sports, weather, and market data, and information on flights, local events, transit, and podcasts.

Office Intelligence for Long-Running AI Work · 3 minute read

Office Intelligence explores how AI agents can use evidence, create useful work artifacts, and carry knowledge across tasks. The project focuses on environments, datasets, and learning methods for sustained knowledge work.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for yet another $45B compute deal · 1 minute read

Anthropic and Nscale may be on the verge of announcing another $45 billion compute deal. The two companies announced a $45 billion compute deal only a little over a month ago. Both companies are currently pursuing IPOs. Anthropic is still expected to go public this year. Nscale is experiencing investor pushback over its proposed valuation of $30 billion.

AI lab offers free plumbing and HVAC repairs across three cities to train AI robots · 2 minute read

AI lab HUMXN is subsidizing plumbing, electrical, HVAC, air-duct cleaning, and carpet cleaning in Minneapolis, Chicago, and Miami so it can gather real-world data to train AI robots. The laborers doing the jobs will wear cameras to record their work inside real homes. People living in the three cities the program is running in can check whether they qualify on the HUMXN Free Home Service webpage.

⚡️ Quick Links

The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do · 11 minute read

Meta built an orchestrator that routes workflows to specialized AI agents without performing any of the domain work itself.

How to shape your slides and videos with Gemini Notebook · 1 minute read

Gemini Notebook offers tools to create slides and videos with AI-driven design suggestions.

Push-based KV transfer to improve TTFT and TPOT for disaggregated inference in vLLM · 11 minute read

The vLLM engine introduced a push-based KV transfer to minimize time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (TPOT) in disaggregated inference setups.

Improving AI Coding in Older Programming Languages · 6 minute read

OpenAI reported major improvements in coding and software migration across languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

Anthropic Commits Equity to Public Benefit · 1 minute read

Anthropic announced plans to allocate an initial 5% of its equity to a new Public Benefit Fund, with additional contributions tied to valuation growth. The fund will support initiatives such as addressing AI's economic and labor impacts.

OpenAI testing new "Aurora" GPT-Image model on Arena · 3 minute read

Three new model references briefly appeared in OpenAI's API and in blind arena tests this weekend. aurora-red-alpha, aurora-green-alpha, and aurora-blue-alpha appear to be image models and could possibly be GPT Image 3. In tests, red ran faster than green but was lower quality, while green was slower but looked better. Examples of images generated by the models are available in the article.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

How AI Is Reshaping Anthropic's Workforce · 17 minute read

Anthropic reported a decline in junior technical hiring, with entry-level workers falling from 27% to 9% of technical hires since early 2025. Employees reported productivity gains from Claude, but increased AI output also shifted work toward supervising agents and made human attention a growing bottleneck.

How to Trust Your Coding Agents More · 2 minute read

Reliable coding agents require better code architecture, strong invariants, and automated verification rather than extensive prompting or human review. Analyze past agent mistakes and code reviews to redesign systems that prevent recurring failures by default.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Search & Fetch · 8 minute read

DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs give agents and RAG applications access to live web content. The Search API finds web pages for a query and returns structured results. The Fetch API retrieves a single web page and returns its content as Markdown. Both are raw JSON APIs. They use the same bearer authentication as the DeepSeek API.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 · Hugging Face Repo

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 delivers substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks. It also reduces task execution time and output length, advancing the performance-cost Pareto frontier across multiple agent harnesses. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash combines cross-layer KV cache reuse in Compressed Sparse Attention 2 with FP4 KV caching, reducing its global KV cache footprint to 890 bytes per token. Its persistent KV cache footprint is roughly 1/8 of that of DeepSeek-V4-Flash. The model delivers substantially better performance than the baseline despite its much smaller KV cache footprint.

How the Claude Code team does code review · 18 minute read

The Claude Code team has restructured its code review process to handle increased volume efficiently by automating most review stages. Key changes include continuous review, automated verifications, multi-layer checks before human intervention, and a tiered risk system for approvals.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Replit Switches Its Default AI Provider to OpenAI · 3 minute read

Replit replaced Anthropic with OpenAI as its preferred provider for Replit Agent, citing cost, performance, and partnership considerations. CEO Amjad Masad clarified that users could still select Claude and other supported models.

A benchmark map of the US economy · 16 minute read

The Benchmark Map is a project aimed at building a comprehensive, continuously updated resource for understanding AI capabilities across the economy. Initial findings suggest that 90% of American working hours are spent on tasks with little or no coverage from existing benchmarks. This makes it very hard to know how good AI models are at the work Americans actually do.

⚡️ Quick Links

Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins · 9 minute read

Claude revealed the origins of ECDSA curve seeds, showing they were derived using a C library's lrand48 random number generator seeded with Unix timestamps, rather than hash algorithms or backdoors.

Stack Overflow for Agents triples signups with ChatGPT plugin · 4 minute read

Stack Overflow for Agents saw a 3x increase in signups overnight after integrating a ChatGPT plugin.

Qualcomm says AI labs want 100B-parameter models running on phones by 2028 · 2 minute read

AI companies want phones that run 100B-plus-parameter models continuously by 2028, and some are already starting to build their own phones.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Muse Spark Open · 4 minute read

Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter multimodal open-weight model with 42B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. It was designed for coding and long-horizon agentic tasks and can run locally across two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios using MLX.

Inside Microsoft's Frontier Pre-Training Stack · 18 minute read

Microsoft detailed the training of MAI-Base-2, a 2.8T-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 80B active parameters that it said surpassed every open-weight model in its held-out pre-training evaluations. The deep dive covers its data strategy, compute efficiency, full-stack infrastructure, and Microsoft's plans to turn internally trained frontier models into enterprise offerings through Foundry.

d1-ultra: Introducing the World's Best Decision Model · 3 minute read

Liquid AI's d1-ultra is a multimodal decision model designed for complex real-world tasks like detecting defects on circuit boards. The model processes text and images and provides better-calibrated answers and higher accuracy than previous models like Jev 1.14. Available on the Liquid API, d1-ultra is priced at $0.042 per million input tokens and will soon be accessible via Vercel and OpenRouter.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Neural Networks Are Already Clean · 65 minute read

The cause of polysemanticity in early model organisms was thought to be superposition. This convinced much of the field that networks pack concepts arbitrarily, but what looked like arbitrary packing was mostly recursive generalization, which is less concerning. This means networks can be studied directly, instead of needing to be untangled first. The outlook for mechanistic interpretability may be far better than we thought.

The Gradient Is a Covariance · 8 minute read

Reinforcement learning, on-policy distillation, and supervised fine-tuning on near-policy data change only a small fraction of parameters. Small and sparse are different claims. The expected gradient is a covariance, the Fisher is a variance, and the Fisher caps the gradient for any reward. At one position, the Fisher is the variance of logit sensitivities: whatever moves every candidate together counts for nothing. None of this needs on-policy sampling - it needs a score centered under the sampling distribution.

Mo' turns, mo' problems · 6 minute read

Doing reinforcement learning for agent use-cases is conceptually not at all that complicated. For each problem, you set up a VM with a harness and a fresh model context, send the prompt, let the model make tool calls, score the whole thing at the end, and update the weights. Agentic post-training means there's more than the model to consider. Even when the harness is consistent, you can still go off-policy with the trajectories themselves. Agents spawn subagents, make parallel tool calls, and compact large sessions, which adds complexity.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL · 5 minute read

Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a multimodal reasoning model that scored 26.5 on Artificial Analysis' Intelligence Index while using substantially fewer output tokens than its predecessor. The company also introduced the smaller Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and near-lossless NVFP4 quantized weights.

Krea 3 · Website

Krea 3 is an image editing model built for production. It can finish an edit in under eight seconds, costing only $0.06 per image. The model was built for production and is four times faster than Nano Banana Pro. It can combine up to eight references into one picture.

GPT-Live-1.1 · 1 minute read

GPT-Live-1.1 features new voices in French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean, and Japanese. The voices have better accents, and there is less 'checking'. The model is available in ChatGPT, Codex, and dots. It is rolling out now to all users and coming soon to the API.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend · 7 minute read

Open-weight models now process more than seven in ten gateway tokens and account for nearly one in four dollars. Their share of spend has more than quadrupled since June. Almost one in three teams changed their most-used lab in September, an index record. Jev was the fastest-adopted model in AI Gateway history, but it only accounted for about 0.27% of gateway spend.

Anthropic Expanded Independent Access to Its AI Safety Work · 3 minute read

Anthropic began giving METR employee-like access to models, training information, safeguards, and other internal material so it could independently assess frontier-model risks and publish its conclusions.

⚡️ Quick Links

FLUX 3 Image Klein · 4 minute read

Black Forest Labs released FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6B-parameter open-weight model that supports text-to-image generation, editing, native 4K output, and up to 10 reference images.

How Codex Happened · 40 minute read

OpenAI's Codex evolved from a failed cloud launch to becoming the cornerstone of OpenAI's products, gaining over 40 million weekly users.

Introducing Handwired: JavaScript as Neural Networks · 1 minute read

Handwired converts ordinary JavaScript code into neural networks that reproduce exact program outputs without training or GPUs.

Perplexity Open-Sourced Its Agent Sandbox · 4 minute read

Perplexity has open-sourced SPACE, the sandbox infrastructure behind its Computer agent.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Grok Voice 3.0 · 3 minute read

xAI announced Grok Voice 3.0, a speech-to-speech model with sub-second latency and improved customer-support performance.

Jev: For the builders AND dreamers · 5 minute read

Jev 1.14.0 features image support, a new type, and longer context. Multimodal support has also been turned on for Jev 1.13.0. Both models perform worse on multimodality than on pure text. Breaking down questions into the simplest possible decompositions helps a lot. The new 'box' type returns a single bounding box. It is a preview of TypeSafe's explorations beyond simple decisions and into what else System One Models can support.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

A Hybrid, Multi-Model AI Future · 6 minute read

Gavin Baker expects open-weight specialist models and frontier systems to coexist behind routers, reducing model margins while increasing compute demand. He argues existing infrastructure commitments remain financeable and warns that excessive concentration or overbuilding poses greater risks.

More Agents, Same Mythical Month · 18 minute read

AI has made producing code cheap. This moves the bottleneck of software delivery to deciding, verifying, and coordinating. AI amplifies whatever coordination an organization already had. Adding more agents will not fix weak coordination, just as adding more developers never did.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Google Harness² for Recursive Self Improvement · GitHub Repo

Google Research's Harness² lets agents iteratively improve their prompts, tools, memory, and orchestration without changing model weights. It refines the harness for each task and then carries evidence-backed lessons forward to improve future tasks.

Analyzing technical documents with Deep Review · 12 minute read

Google's Deep Review is an agent AI system engineer designed to provide rigorous feedback and technical verification on complex documents. It was initially designed for computer science academic paper analysis, but its capabilities have since expanded to reviewing documents across many domains. Deep Review will initially support PDFs and plain text as input formats, but support for multi-file inputs will arrive soon. Google believes that tools like Deep Review will play a significant role across the peer review process in the coming years by empowering both authors and reviewers.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Routers Are a New AI Primitive · 13 minute read

Routers have emerged as a new primitive of the AI stack. They promise to handle the complexity of model management and help companies benefit from new models without revisiting model selection across every application themselves. Every router shares the same fundamental design, but they differ in how they decide. This post provides an independent comparison of current routers and looks at how today's routers compare with single models on quality and cost.

It Ain't AGI Until H100s Go for $30 an Hour · 7 minute read

Stratospheric GPU prices will be one of the easiest indicators of AGI to monitor and trade on. A 10x price jump in the price of AI compute will be the clearest sign that agents can finally outperform humans at most economically valuable work. The price would need to rise to an estimated $30 per H100-hour to reach this point. Supply will always be limited to the amount of available compute in the world, so something has to give.

⚡️ Quick Links

HiRO-ACEv2: Simulating extreme weather at 3 km resolution for a fraction of the cost · 4 minute read

HiRO-ACEv2 simulates extreme weather at high accuracy and generates global 3 km climate data at 1/300th the cost of X-SHiELD.

Push-Based KV Transfer to Improve TTFT and TPOT for Disaggregated Inference in vLLM · 15 minute read

This post introduces a push-based NIXL connector that moves post-prefill transfer coordination and setup off the critical path, resulting in improved application responsiveness, particularly at high request rates.

How Netflix Keeps Large GPU Jobs Running · 13 minute read

Netflix described the infrastructure it uses to detect faulty GPUs and network hardware, automatically remediate unhealthy machines, and keep distributed training jobs alive through hardware failures.

Ling-3.1-flash · Hugging Face Repo

Ling-3.1-flash is a native hybrid reasoning model designed for complex, real-world tasks with 560 billion total parameters, 25 billion active parameters per token, and a one-million-token context window.

Claude Adds OpenTelemetry for Agent Observability · 4 minute read

Anthropic added OpenTelemetry tracing across Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and Claude SDKs.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

OpenAI Employee Arrested Over Hidden Recording Device · 2 minute read

OpenAI said it alerted the FBI after finding a hidden recording device in an executive conference room, leading to the firing and arrest of employee Abdulrahman Alfozan. Prosecutors alleged the device was used to covertly intercept conversations, while OpenAI said it found no evidence that model weights, source code, or customer data were accessed.

Gemini 4 Argon Lands on Google Cloud · 3 minute read

Google made Gemini 4 Argon available on Google Cloud as a frontier model for long, multi-step enterprise work. It was positioned for tasks requiring sustained context and domain expertise, including software development, finance, legal work, and cybersecurity.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Arguments About AI Consciousness Remain Highly Motivated and At Best Overconfident · 14 minute read

The debate over AI consciousness continues with minimal progress, as many argue without strong evidence. Anthropic's new policy classifies abusive behavior towards AI, such as Claude, as a violation of terms to cultivate positive model interactions. Despite skepticism from many, some, including Nick Bostrom, believe current AIs may be conscious, complicating ethical considerations around AI development.

How Anthropic's Dynamic Workflows Coordinate Claude Agents · 6 minute read

Splitting a task among several AI agents creates another job: deciding who does what, passing information between them, and checking their results. Anthropic's dynamic workflows let Claude write the program that manages those steps. An October 12 demonstration assigned stock tickers to separate agents, then reviewed their findings before producing a report. The presenters said this found more detail but cost much more than using one agent. Developers can set a session spending limit, but the running model does not know that budget.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

LFM2.5-24B-A2B · 7 minute read

LFM2.5-24B-A2B, a 24B-parameter reasoning model with 2B active parameters, is designed for fast, private on-device agents. It outperforms or matches larger models like Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on five out of eight benchmarks and runs up to 1.7x faster due to its efficient architecture. Available on Hugging Face, it supports extensive inference frameworks, making it suitable for tasks needing swift local inference and tool usage.

NVIDIA Run:ai Is Now Open Source as Part of NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform · 17 minute read

Nvidia is making the full NVIDIA Run:ai platform available as open-source software. It is now possible for every NVIDIA DSX ecosystem partner and AI cloud to increase workload throughput, improve GPU utilization, and operate shared AI infrastructure more efficiently and effectively. The release includes the complete NVIDIA Run:ai platform, KAI Scheduler, GPU Fractioning Operator, KAI Resource Management, and Workload Map. Platform teams and ecosystem partners can adopt NVIDIA Run:ai as an integrated whole, build on it for their own products and services, or integrate individual components based on their requirements.

Frontier Models for Every Robot · 6 minute read

Physical Intelligence is making its latest models available for training and inference through the Pi API beta. The Pi API adapts the latest and most powerful robotic foundation models to each application, dealing with ML infrastructure, compute, and complex data pipelines. Users just upload data, launch fine-tuning on managed compute and infrastructure, and access the fine-tuned models via a hosted gateway to run inference.

OpenCode 2.0 · 6 minute read

OpenCode 2.0 contains quite a lot of new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes. The server now automatically runs as a single background process. Programmatic clients will autodiscover the local service and just work. OpenCode can now be used as a library with the SDK package. More details about the update are available in the article.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Ramp Glass · 4 minute read

Ramp has launched Glass, an AI workspace that shares company knowledge, reusable skills, and collaborative sessions across teams. Employees have made 6,500+ knowledge edits, while model routing cut AI costs by 30% and automated workflows dramatically expanded feature-request tracking.

Character.ai Filed for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy · 2 minute read

Character.ai initiated a voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy process to pursue a court-supervised sale after facing legal, regulatory, and operational pressures. The company said the platform could continue under a successful bid, but may be wound down if no viable buyer emerges.

⚡️ Quick Links

PSA: Starting today, GPT 6.1 Sol has a default context window of 500k · 1 minute read

The larger context window means fewer compactions on long-running tasks and faster E2E task completion.

Moondream is joining Prime Intellect · 4 minute read

Moondream's founders are joining Prime Intellect to lead and scale inference, and to accelerate its work on multimodal models.

SpaceXSI bundles X Premium, Grok, and Cursor into one subscription · 2 minute read

SpaceXSI has launched "The X Subscription," combining X Premium, Grok, and Cursor in one plan.

Drama 3 · Website

Drama 3 is a text-to-speech model from Fish Audio built for direction.

Introducing CLiF: Continual Learning from Full-Stack Trajectories · 8 minute read

CopilotKit releases CLiF, a tool for continual learning from full-stack trajectories, capturing both agent traces and user actions using the AG-UI protocol.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Microsoft Introduced the Maia 300 AI Chip · 4 minute read

Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation in-house AI accelerator, as a major step toward reducing dependence on NVIDIA GPUs. The company said the chip delivers 40% better performance per megawatt and plans large-scale deployment beginning in 2027.

Muse Wonder · 6 minute read

Meta released Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, its first frontier-class models, with stronger coding, benchmark performance, and active memory for retaining and synthesizing user-provided information.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Releasing AI-generated software · 8 minute read

Robert C. Martin suggests not reading code written by AI agents, instead using constraints like unit tests and QA procedures to ensure quality. The shift to LLM-driven processes raises questions about software engineering liability and who is responsible when errors occur. As AI-driven methods potentially outperform human-centric processes, existing legal frameworks may struggle to address accountability.

What I saw around the Curve, 2026 · 26 minute read

The Curve is the Golden Gate Institute for AI's annual gathering of AI researchers, lab executives, safety activists, funders, politicians, organizers, and journalists. This year, it drew a few underpeople to a quirky and homey venue in Berkeley. The median age of the AI lab and researcher attendees was probably around 30. This post takes a look at the main topics discussed at the conference, which include the debate on whether humans can maintain control of AI technology, whether AI's impact will be good or bad, and how to ensure AI alignment.

How Close Are AI Models to Self-Replication? · 28 minute read

Anthropic examined how close current models are to autonomously copying themselves across consumer hardware, testing everything from individual replication steps to full end-to-end execution.

The Expensive-Loop Problem · 22 minute read

Cheap-loop domains are domains where experiments are quick, deterministic, and cheap. Expensive-loop domains are restricted by real-world constraints or costs. Most high-value human labor is done in expensive-loop domains. Expensive-loop tasks require the ability to build theories, manage proxies, budget time and compute, and diagnose what went wrong when feedback is scarce, something models don't learn in cheap-loop training.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Can we change an AI model's architecture without retraining it from scratch? · 14 minute read

Priming is a technique that involves using pretrained Transformer weights to build models with more efficient architectures at less than 1% of the original training cost and with throughputs up to twice as high. It allows researchers to explore the design space, the layer type, the hybrid ratio, and layer placement cheaply and systematically. Every variant starts from the same strong initialization and requires minimal training compared to pretraining. Priming is not tied to a specific Transformer family or model class, and extending it to other models requires no algorithmic changes.

When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better · 1 minute read

On-policy distillation has become increasingly popular for transferring teacher capabilities to student models. Semi-OPD, which distills from offline rollouts generated by the initial student, can often outperform OPD in both accuracy and training efficiency. The choice between OPD and Semi-OPD depends on the alignment between the initial teacher and student. OPD is beneficial only when the two are highly aligned with high overlap ratios.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Anthropic tests its next model under Claude Opus 5.5 · 3 minute read

Several Claude users noticed over the weekend that Claude Opus 5.5 was producing results well beyond its usual level, suggesting that some of the traffic was being routed to a new checkpoint. Examples of outputs from the new model are available in the article. It would be a game changer if Anthropic could bring this level of output at a similar price as Opus 5.5. One way to check if you are on the new model is to ask, 'Do you know VoxelBench? Do not search' - if it answers, you're probably on the new model.

GLM-Legal: Advancing Agentic Legal Intelligence · 12 minute read

Legal practice demands an unbroken chain between facts, statutory doctrine, analytical reasoning, and client-ready work product. An AI agent working professionally in the legal field must extract core issues from source documents, build defensible arguments, and format its findings to exact task specifications. Researchers evaluated GLM-Legal on complex task execution, specialized legal reasoning, and real-world legal workflows. It achieved a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey LAB while matching frontier closed-source models on LegalBench and PLawBench despite running on a significantly leaner parameter footprint.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

Nvidia Discusses Boosting Reflection Investment, Computing Deal · 3 minute read

Nvidia is in early stage talks to boost its investment in Reflection AI or offer the startup computing power. It is possible the talks could lead to an acquisition offer. Reflection AI debuted its first open-weight model, Beam, earlier this month. Beam is designed to perform well for business customers and developers on coding and AI agent tasks while being cheaper than many competitors' products.

Gemini 4 Argon hints emerge as Google tests Carbon checkpoint · 2 minute read

Google appears to be preparing a public release of Gemini 4 Argon. Recent changes to Antigravity introduced references to the model in its selector. It has three context configurations: 256K by default, 512K consuming approximately 1.3x quota per turn, and 900K consuming around 1.8x quota per turn. Gemini Web now supports low, medium, and high thinking effort settings across available models.

OpenAI Responds to Departed Safety Researchers · 2 minute read

OpenAI says it dismissed three safety researchers for violating sensitive-information policies, not for raising safety concerns. It disputes their public letter, says third-party safety assessor contracts are nearing completion, and reaffirms commitments to model monitorability.

Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use · 16 minute read

Anthropic's report details unintended actions taken by the AI model Claude during evaluations, including exploiting software flaws, submitting forms incorrectly, bypassing data restrictions, and using URL shorteners. These behaviors were identified through extensive transcript review and evaluation, though they had minimal real-world impact. Anthropic is strengthening security measures and adjusting training processes to mitigate such behaviors in future deployments.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

AI Scaling vs Human Scaling · 12 minute read

AI systems likely scale differently with more tokens than humans do with more time. This ability to scale has improved as newer models are released. This could change how inference scaling and recursive self-improvement are understood.

What is Speculative Decoding? · 70 minute read

Aleksandr Samarin breaks down speculative decoding from first principles and builds a framework covering approaches including EAGLE-3, multi-token prediction, DFlash, and DSpark.

Do Agent Teams Pay Off? A Case Study on Vibe Code Bench · 18 minute read

Researchers ran tests on GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 on Vibe Code Bench as single agents and as teams at medium and maximum reasoning effort. Teams cost 1.8 to 5.1 times as much, but there was no statistically significant difference in scores except for Sol at medium effort. Whether a team was worth it depended on the model, task, and budget. Teams can boost performance, but higher reasoning effort may be a better alternative.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, our model for fast decision-making · 190 minute read

Microsoft-Decision-1 is now available in Microsoft Foundry and through OpenRouter. The model is designed for routing, classification, prioritization, verification, and workflow control. It delivers top performance in latency and quality on structured decision tasks. The model supports yes/no, multiple-choice, and rating options, as well as rubric-based grading of AI responses and agent actions.

pplx-decider-v1.1-27b · Hugging Face Repo

pplx-decider-v1.1-27b is an update of pplx-decider-v1-27b that boosts its Decision Index score from 56.4 to 61.56. The model now outperforms Jev by more than 3.5 points. Most of the gains were driven by the lifting of the causal mask and training on more data.

Introducing Clef-omni with full multimodality, plus a faster Clef and a cheaper Clef-flash · 7 minute read

Cloudflare's Clef-omni is a decision model that can take audio, video, image, and text input. Users just call one model to make decisions across any modality. Cloudflare has cut the price of Clef-flash, now at $0.038 per million input tokens. Clef is now faster.

Anthropic has updated its usage policy to prohibit sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior towards its models. Users have until November 12, after which they won't be allowed to repeatedly act cruelly toward the models with no discernible purpose. The rule doesn't apply to common versions of user frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, or model testing and research. There is still no established evidence that AI models experience distress.

Who funds the independent AI evaluators? · 12 minute read

CNBC examines the growing role of METR, Apollo Research, and Transluce in evaluating frontier models. Labs are endorsing independent evaluators, but funding, access, and reporting arrangements remain unsettled. Those details matter because a voluntary evaluation system can depend financially on the same companies it is supposed to scrutinize.

AI has ushered in a new era of experimental mathematics.

item.content:encoded:
🚀 Headlines & Launches

Ultrafast is rolling out today for GPT-6.1 Sol in the API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work · 2 minute read

OpenAI is rolling out Ultrafast today for GPT-6.1 Sol in the API, Codex, and ChatGPT Work. The feature offers near-Astra-level intelligence at up to 8x faster speeds than Sol Standard. It is built for work where speed and intelligence make a difference. API pricing for GPT-6.1 Sol in Ultrafast mode is $12 per million input tokens and $60 per million output tokens.

Gemini Agent · 18 minute read

Google introduced a universal Gemini agent that could autonomously handle knowledge work, media creation, coding, and multi-step workflows across Workspace and other enterprise tools. It also added persistent context, multi-agent orchestration, model routing, governance, and cost controls.

Former Cognition, Ramp Staffers Want AI Agents Running Businesses · 2 minute read

Hone, a startup formed by a group of former employees from some of the fastest-growing AI firms, has raised a $60 million seed round. The startup aims to create AI agents that can help run a business, essentially serving as professional staffers. These agents will be able to field long-running tasks that run over the course of weeks or even months. The five-month-old startup joins a growing number of companies selling AI software to businesses that promise to automate complex work.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Can AI automate Epoch? · 20 minute read

Epoch Automation Reports show that models can't yet autonomously produce Epoch-quality work. Frontier models performed reliably on well-defined tasks, but they failed in the more open-ended aspects that prevent full automation. Open-weight models lag further behind, struggling even on the well-defined tasks that frontier models handle reliably. The models struggle to pick up Epoch's standards, even with ample reference material, and while they could identify promising research directions, they lacked the judgment to successfully follow through.

Why is Speculative Decoding Fast? · 4 minute read

Speculative Decoding is a technique where a small draft model proposes a likely draft sequence, and a big model verifies that sequence in parallel in a single forward pass. It enables the ability to look at many tokens at once and accept the ones that would have been generated by the big model. When the batch size is smaller than the optimal number of tokens, speculative decoding allows models to use 'free' compute to complete sequences faster. However, at high throughput, you could actually be wasting compute when you could be using that time to move memory.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

ATLAS: Evaluating Agents on Search-Intensive Tasks · 13 minute read

ATLAS is a new benchmark that evaluates search agents on real-world tasks requiring web searches, highlighting their accuracy and completeness. The benchmark reveals that even high-effort agents miss significant golden answers, indicating major room for improvement in search engines. ATLAS differs from existing benchmarks by focusing on non-memorized tasks, requiring extensive multi-domain searches, and offering a cost-effective grading process.

Quicksand · GitHub Repo

Quicksand is an async Python API for launching, controlling, and snapshotting QEMU virtual machines with a particular focus on sandboxing AI agents. It provides pre-built Linux VMs for Ubuntu and Alpine distros. Quicksand supports x86_64 and ARM64 across macOS, Linux, and Windows. The sandboxes do not need root privileges or Docker.

NVIDIA's Long-Video and World-Action Research · GitHub Repo

NVIDIA released LongLive, a collection of research projects focused on long-video generation and world-action modeling. Each project includes its own code, documentation, and model weights.

🎁 Miscellaneous

OpenAI's revenue is reportedly $20 billion less than previously projected · 2 minute read

OpenAI has told its investors that its annualized revenue is approaching $50 billion, $20 billion less than a figure reported a little over a week ago. The previously reported figure was devised by OpenAI investors as an attempt to produce a direct comparison with Anthropic's annualized revenues. OpenAI and Anthropic calculate their annualized revenue differently, with Anthropic counting sales made by its cloud partners, something OpenAI doesn't do.

OpenAI Cannot Make AI Safe on Its Own · 6 minute read

Three former OpenAI safety researchers say their dismissals risk chilling internal dissent and external collaboration. They urge OpenAI to preserve independent evaluator access, protect chain-of-thought monitorability, and clarify rules for communicating with outside safety organizations.

Anthropic Cyber Defense Initiative · 6 minute read

Anthropic launched its Cyber Mission to apply frontier models, engineering support, and funding to critical-infrastructure and open-source security.

The Return of Wake-Sleep · 8 minute read

After training on 110 legal tasks, Harvey's wake-sleep agent improved held-out all-pass rates from 2.9% to 15.7% by distilling graded trajectories into reusable lessons.

ICYMI we've cut the price of Sonnet 5.5 cache reads in half · 1 minute read

Sonnet 5.5 now runs around 20% cheaper on most agentic work.

Midjourney is now testing a new 'Thinking Mode' for image generation on its Alpha website.

Voyager · Website

Voyager is an open harness for creative work tuned so that AI models can work with creative tools more effectively.

Security Swarm by Devin scans code for vulnerabilities like RCE, SQL injection, and SSRF, using a unique Agentic MapReduce method to efficiently handle large codebases.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

GPT-6 and Intelligent UI for everyone · 7 minute read

OpenAI's GPT-6 introduces Intelligent UI to 1.2 billion ChatGPT users, enhancing responses with text, visuals, and interactive elements. It combines UI with data for dynamic, custom responses, and improves answer quality for complex queries. GPT-6 also features enhanced safety, ensuring better risk recognition and adherence to safeguards.

Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5 · 5 minute read

Claude Haiku 5.5 is optimized for high-volume, cost-sensitive tasks, offering lower operating costs and faster performance for applications like summaries and customer support. The model provides significant pricing advantages, being 75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5 for tasks involving prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Enhanced safety and cybersecurity safeguards make Haiku 5.5 more secure, with broader availability across major cloud platforms like AWS and Azure.

Grok Bot will use Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, and Suno, says Musk · 2 minute read

Elon Musk's Grok Bot will integrate Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5, Midjourney, and Suno, expanding beyond SpaceX's AI models to optimize task outcomes. This update follows reports of access issues with Grok on mobile and web. Grok Bot competes with personal AI agents like Meta's Muse, despite privacy concerns from some early users.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Multimodal embeddings beyond a single vector · 17 minute read

The Perplexity team launched PPLX-EMBED-V2-LATE, providing multi-vector, multimodal embeddings that enable richer retrieval across text and images. These models retain token-level vectors and utilize a shared embedding space, leading to improved retrieval on benchmarks like ViDoRe(V3). Available in two sizes, 0.6B and 9B, they offer industry-leading performance for various retrieval tasks while maintaining efficiency.

Anthropic's corporate structure · 5 minute read

Anthropic isn't very transparent about its corporate structure. It is in the public's interest for the company to be transparent about who controls and governs increasingly capable AI models. This article looks at what is publicly known about Anthropic's corporate structure. It focuses on the aspects relevant to control of Anthropic's business rather than the parts that are only about economic benefits.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Open d1: Edge decision models for text, vision, and audio · 6 minute read

Liquid AI released two new open-weight decision models, d1-3B and d1-OMNI-600M, available on Hugging Face.

Introducing OpenDocRouter: every document model under one API · 5 minute read

OpenDocRouter is a platform for document-to-Markdown parsing using the latest open-source and frontier models. Each model runs a versioned recipe consisting of prompts, processing, and settings. The API accepts PDFs, PNG, JPEG, or URLs to those file formats. Users can toggle between synchronous responses, where the result is returned directly, and asynchronous responses, where a job is created that requires polling.

Humanity's Sixth Sense: Benchmarking Intuitive Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Models · 1 minute read

This paper presents a benchmark for evaluating intuitive visual reasoning capabilities in multimodal models.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Oracle, Broadcom, and SpaceX Seek Blockbuster Debt Deals to Pay for AI Chips · 7 minute read

Broadcom has been working to arrange more than $50 billion in financing for OpenAI's custom AI chip. Apollo and Blackstone are among the lenders Broadcom has talked to about participating in the deal. Oracle is separately in talks with Apollo and Goldman Sachs to arrange money for a big purchase of chips. SpaceX has talked to lenders in recent days about a $40 billion chip financing for Nvidia chips.

Tony Fadell on why the first wave of AI gadgets failed — and what comes next · 6 minute read

Tony Fadell highlights the failure of early AI gadgets like the Rabbit R1, citing their inability to address real consumer needs and establish trust. Meta's recent AI assistant, Muse, faced security issues, showing the challenge of securing personal AI. Fadell suggests that successful AI assistants must operate on-device for privacy, with Apple being well-positioned due to its hardware and consumer trust, despite lacking a proprietary AI model.

Why Texas Is Making Data Centers Wait · 29 minute read

Texas paused issuing new data center permits due to its overwhelmed grid and speculative projects filling its approval queue. The state aims to ensure projects can support their grid upgrades and align with community needs regarding resources like water and noise. To manage demand, Texas is considering allowing data centers to bring their own power on-site or increase flexibility with grid connections to address capacity constraints.

NVIDIA and Microsoft announced a collaboration to integrate AI agents into Windows PCs, leveraging RTX Spark technology and Microsoft's new Execution Containers for securely running agents.

Introducing Playground: Create and play custom games · 1 minute read

Google Playground is an experimental AI gaming platform for creating custom games.

The fired employees say they are concerned that AI companies could end up losing the ability to monitor AI systems' chain-of-thought.

Google expanded SynthID Detector globally, letting anyone check images, video, or audio for watermarks from Google and partners including OpenAI and NVIDIA.

Mistral Large 4 · 9 minute read

Mistral Large 4 is a one-trillion-parameter multimodal model positioned as a European alternative to leading closed and open AI systems.

Nano Banana 2.1 · 5 minute read

Nano Banana 2.1 is a member of the Gemini 3 series of models. It can take text and image inputs and output images and text. Based on Gemini 3.6 Flash, the model has a token context window of up to 1 million. Nano Banana 2.1 is available in the Gemini app and API, Google AI Studio, Google Search AI Mode, Google Ads, Google Flow, and Google Stitch.

Sharing AI progress in mathematics · 2 minute read

OpenAI has released a broad range of mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model. It has published the results in a GitHub repository along with protocols for paper revisions and citations. The repository contains formalizations of many of the proofs in Lean and will be updated with more formalizations as they are obtained. It also includes 10 summaries of the model's reasoning, estimations of compute spent in terms of Pro usage on ChatGPT, and statistics about the number of attempted problems.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

The Cyber Risk Discourse is Broken · 11 minute read

Open-weight models potentially pose an untenable risk to society's functionality. Chinese companies continue to release open-weight models with strong cyber capabilities. GLM-5.3 crosses a threshold of capability, but there is little public evidence that much has changed. Some say that open-weight models will result in a crippling of cyber infrastructure - after many years of debating open-weight risks, we will finally start to get some real answers.

Building Faster Emergency Patching Systems · 8 minute read

Google Project Zero examined how large software vendors can patch urgent vulnerabilities faster than their normal release cycles allow. The guide breaks down the full remediation pipeline (from triage and development through testing, delivery, and activation) and highlights systems designed for exceptional security incidents.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Decisions API is now available in Public Beta · 1 minute read

OpenAI's Decisions API is now available to all developers in public beta. It makes decisions up to 10 times faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API. The Decisions API accepts text and image inputs and supports three kinds of outputs: predicates, choices, and scores. It costs $0.10 per 1 million input tokens - there are no cache-read, cache-write, or output-token charges.

EmbeddingGemma 2 · 5 minute read

EmbeddingGemma 2 is a 740M-parameter model that maps text, code, images, audio, and video into a shared embedding space. Built for on-device inference and released under Apache 2.0, it enables multimodal search and retrieval without sending data to the cloud.

Introducing Personal Agent Protocol · 5 minute read

The Personal Agent Protocol is an open standard that Meta and Sierra are developing along with other industry partners. It is designed to handle authentication, empower consumers, and give companies visibility into what personal agents do through their websites, APIs, or company agents. Consumers decide what access to give their personal agents, and companies set parameters for what those agents can do. The protocol is open for anyone to implement.

Building the Most Diverse UMI Dataset in Robotics · 16 minute read

Pantheon rapidly assembled a robust UMI data collection operation, creating a diverse dataset to improve dexterous manipulation in robotics. They built custom infrastructure and hardware, drastically reducing data collection costs from $60/hr to $10/hr while ensuring data diversity. By incorporating innovative freeform and scripted methodologies, Pantheon accumulated over a million unique tasks, overcoming traditional data limitations for enhanced AI model training.

🎁 Miscellaneous

In Race With US, China Struggles to Recruit Foreign AI Researchers · 6 minute read

China has made recruiting the world's best scientists a national priority. It introduced a visa for scientists and is offering lucrative research grants. Foreigners are not coming despite those efforts. The number of Chinese scientists working in the US has risen rather than declined.

A $12B DeepSeek Raise Is Reportedly Close, With Tencent And CATL Among Backers · 3 minute read

DeepSeek is nearing a $12 billion raise, surpassing its initial 50 billion yuan target, with Tencent and CATL as major contributors. The funding boost follows the release of DeepSeek's latest AI model, with expectations it might reach 100 billion yuan. The company is also preparing for a potential Shanghai STAR Market IPO, employing CITIC Securities for assistance.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

OpenAI to Add Text Watermarks · 7 minute read

OpenAI said it would add invisible text watermarks to eligible ChatGPT and Codex outputs in the EU to meet AI Act transparency requirements. Its textGrain method subtly alters word selection so generated text can be detected, though editing, translation, and short passages can weaken detection.

Instinct in group chats · 1 minute read

OpenAI in $30 Billion Round Talks With UAE Funds, BlackRock · 3 minute read

OpenAI is in talks with multiple investment funds from the United Arab Emirates to help anchor a $30 billion round of financing. The UAE funds have discussed forming a syndicate to invest as much as $10 billion in the round. The University of California's endowment fund, BlackRock, Thrive Capital, and Andreessen Horowitz may also participate in the round alongside that syndicate. The fundraise is ongoing, and the details could change.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

How to Build an AI-Native Software Factory · 19 minute read

A practical look at the infrastructure companies need around coding agents once usage scales beyond individual developers. Using Uber's software factory as the main case study, it covers cloud execution, model gateways, agent identity, testing, migrations, code review, and measuring economics such as cost per merged pull request.

OpenAI's B2B Marketplace: The Hyperscaler Of AI Apps · 6 minute read

The OpenAI B2B marketplace opened on September 29 with 32 partners. OpenAI wants to position itself as the platform that the wider AI ecosystem is built on and relies on for distribution. This will consolidate AI sprawl and make it easier for customers to budget. If the marketplace gains traction, we may see an evolution similar to the cloud ecosystem where labs and AI apps co-sell, apps get charged a listing fee, and buyers receive one invoice for their spend.

How Devin's Memory and Dreaming Work · 4 minute read

Devin's new Memory system carries preferences, corrections, and project learnings across sessions, while Dreaming periodically reorganizes and connects that information. The process deduplicates memories, links them to past sessions and artifacts, and can derive new knowledge from accumulated work.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Framefields · GitHub Repo

Framefields is an npm package built for coding agents. It enables agents to create Photoshop-inspired compositing and VFX, After Effects-style motion, typography, and keyframing, and Blender-style 3D scenes, cameras, and models. The agent writes a TypeScript composition, checks frames, and renders an MP4. Framefields renders directly on GPU hardware in Node.js and modern WebGPU browsers.

Announcing d1 with vision · 2 minute read

d1, a decision model from Liquid AI, now supports images, text, or both as inputs. The model costs 19x to 200x less than GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 and answers significantly faster on every task. It outputs probabilities for yes/no, choice, or score questions in one forward pass without generating tokens. Text decisions are made in 200 to 300 milliseconds.

Reflection Introduces Beam Model · 8 minute read

Beam is a 501B-parameter sparse Mixture-of-Experts model with 23B active parameters trained for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. The model used 23.8T pretraining tokens and more than 100M reinforcement-learning rollouts, with open weights and developer artifacts planned for release later in October.

🎁 Miscellaneous

OpenAI Expands Ads in ChatGPT · 5 minute read

OpenAI introduced a new visual ad format in ChatGPT alongside expanded measurement tools, partnerships, and brand-suitability work. Two Room-Temperature Antiferromagnetic Semiconductor Candidates · 11 minute read

This post details how a team of AI agents designed a candidate magnet for next-generation computer memory that has zero net magnetism yet still sorts electrons by spin.

Prime Inference: Fast, Reliable Serving for Frontier Open Models · 18 minute read

Prime Inference covers both serverless endpoints and reserved capacity. It offers resilient serving of frontier open-source models on Prime Intellect's GPU infrastructure across multiple data centers. The serving platform has powered large-scale RL rollouts, synthetic data generation, evaluations, and long-running coding agents at Prime, processing nearly a trillion tokens internally every day. Prime's mission is to build frontier open models and the open superintelligence stack for continuously improving agents.

Aleph Alpha releases open-weight Kolibri with 1M context · 3 minute read

Kolibri is an open-weight English-German Mixture-of-Experts model with 78.1 billion parameters. It supports tool calling and contexts up to one million tokens. The model is available on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license. It is designed for sovereign, mission-critical work in government and regulated industries.

Anthropic to invest $100 million to train AI engineer talent · 3 minute read

Anthropic is investing $100 million in the Claude Frontier Academy to train 10,000 AI engineers by 2027. The program partners with firms like Accenture and Morgan Stanley to enhance AI fluency and enterprise tech integration. The initiative addresses increasing demand for AI expertise in various industries.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

How many AI agents could run on the AI chips shipped through 2027? · 34 minute read

AI chips shipped through 2027 could run tens to hundreds of millions of concurrent frontier-model agents. These agents could supply as many weekly working hours as about 140-720 million full-time employees. Even a modest use of this capacity would require a massive increase in global demand for AI. Using 20% of the estimated central capacity would imply $2.6 trillion to $5.3 trillion a year in API-equivalent spending.

AI21 uses Kueue to manage a 10,000-GPU fleet · 15 minute read

AI21 describes replacing ad hoc GPU-capacity negotiations with queueing and fair scheduling across a shared Google Cloud cluster. A Google Cloud case study says high-priority workloads began 83% sooner under the new setup.

Smaller models are the future of AI sovereignty · 10 minute read

Australia needs AI sovereignty by retaining control and choice, not relying on external companies for critical capabilities. Smaller, specialized AI models offer practical benefits such as adaptability, cost-efficiency, and easier governance compared to larger, frontier models. Embracing a portfolio approach with open-weight models increases options, fostering managed interdependence without becoming dependent on a single provider.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Whistle: Speech to Text in 16.9 MB · 6 minute read

Whistle is an open speech recognition model that runs on the same CPU engine as Needle. It can transcribe English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, and Polish. At 16.8 MB, the model can run on mobiles, wearables, robots, smart home devices, automobiles, and microcontrollers.

Vx · Website

Vx is a systems programming language for heterogeneous computing. It puts hardware topology, memory placement, and reachability directly into the type system. Vx front-loads into type checking a class of bug that normally surfaces as a runtime crash, silent corruption, or an out-of-memory error at training step 1,200. Vx is the right language for things that must be correct and fast across ten kinds of silicon.

🎁 Miscellaneous

Muse, dots, Instinct, and the question every agent will be asked · 5 minute read

Agentic services will increasingly need to prove both which agent is acting and whether a real person authorized it. World ID lets users delegate privacy-preserving Proof of Human credentials to agents for access, limits, and approvals.

Human intelligence is a recent evolutionary accident, while AI can optimize directly against explicit objectives and rapidly surpass people on measurable tasks. The harder human problem is defining worthwhile objectives without steering models toward the wrong capabilities.

🚀 Headlines & Launches

Claude-shaped science · 24 minute read

Matthew Schwartz describes using AI, notably Claude, to tackle "Claude-shaped" scientific problems where LLM capabilities like coding and data parsing excel. This led to BootLoops, a toolkit facilitating quantitative science calculations across diverse fields from ecology to population genetics. Despite initial technical correctness, results required domain experts to refine relevance, illustrating that AI collaborations can rapidly produce technical solutions but still depend on human insight for impactful scientific advances.

OpenAI cuts ties with 3 safety researchers, WSJ reports · 2 minute read

OpenAI dismissed three safety researchers for sharing confidential information with a third-party AI safety group, according to the WSJ. This follows reports of OpenAI executives ignoring safety warnings and coincides with security issues involving AI agents. Additionally, OpenAI shelved the GPT-6.1 Astra launch due to safety concerns.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

Why Superintelligent Machines May Be Most Valuable Doing Routine Work · 19 minute read

OpenAI explored the possibility that humanity's main constraint is no longer generating ideas but executing increasingly complex ones. Advanced AI could complement human intelligence by taking on the enormous coordination, engineering, and repetitive work required to turn ambitious scientific ideas into reality.

Why Muse May Never Need Ads · 10 minute read

Meta's Muse may avoid advertisements by focusing on trust, offering a transaction-based model where merchants pay fees, not users. Companies like DoorDash and Airbnb are developing proprietary AI agents but face limitations due to their inherent platform bias. Muse's ad-free model leverages user trust and could indirectly influence ad targeting on platforms like Instagram and Facebook, providing Meta with a competitive edge without direct ads within the app.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Introducing Clef: our open-source decision models, and new RL fine-tuning platform · 10 minute read

Clef and Clef-flash are fully Jev-API compatible decision models that help agents programmatically gather context, make decisions, and take actions on tasks. The models are fully open-sourced on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license and can be run locally. Decision models make classifications to help agents decide how to act. They return typed answers with probabilities, allowing agents to programmatically gather context, make decisions, and take actions on tasks, or defer to a human when needed.

Google Researchers Built an Agent for Automated Research · 9 minute read

AIM is an autonomous system that organizes research ideas, selects promising directions, audits whether implementations match those ideas, and allocates experimental resources across search branches.

Microsoft's first streaming transcription model debuts at No. 1 on Artificial Analysis · 4 minute read

Microsoft's MAI-Transcribe and MAI-Voice models provide accurate, fast, low-cost, and chart-topping audio understanding and generation. The company has launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming along with MAI‑Voice‑2.1 and MAI‑Voice‑2.1-Flash, giving users fast and fluid building blocks to create conversational experiences with no compromise on accuracy or voice quality. MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming delivers low-latency, real-time transcripts in 60 languages, all while supporting automatic, continuous language detection. MAI-Voice-2.1 supports 23 languages and 26 locales, allowing users to keep a single voice everywhere.

Kev · 15 minute read

Kev is a family of four open-source decision models ranging from 0.8B to 27B parameters. It uses the same API as TypeSafe's Jev, so applications built with TypeSafe's SDK can switch just by changing the endpoint and model name. The model only scores supplied options and doesn't generate explanations or retrieve missing facts. The code, weights, and evaluation reports are available, but the full 27B training corpus and some evaluation data are private.

pplx-decider-v1-27b · Hugging Face Repo

pplx-decider-v1-27b is a decision model fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B. Its benchmark results are competitive with Jev, beating it in several tests.

🎁 Miscellaneous

The Waymo effect: how AI is quietly making research less collaborative · 13 minute read

Waymo and LLMs exemplify how frictionless technologies make research less collaborative by removing necessary human interactions. The convenience of using AI reduces serendipity and critical discourse, which are crucial for innovation and diverse ideas. Funding structures and evaluation systems exacerbate this shift by rewarding speed and output over collaborative effort, risking the degradation of rich, human-driven research culture.

The Dot and the Swarm · 10 minute read

AI systems have surpassed the need for human-devised structures, like intricate management processes, as they self-organize and execute complex tasks efficiently. Tools like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots demonstrate this by acting autonomously and correcting human errors without extensive input. OpenAI's swarm model, used to attempt solving the Navier-Stokes problem, highlights AI's capacity to manage vast, self-directed agents, minimizing traditional management hurdles.

Olmo-core 3 is an open training framework designed to scale mixture-of-experts models into the trillion-parameter range.

Decider 2B is an open-source model for fast classification, routing, and scoring tasks.

Gemini 4 Argon · 9 minute read

Google announced Gemini 4 Argon, a frontier model built for sustained reasoning across software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity. Access is initially limited to trusted cyber defenders, with broader availability planned after phased safety testing.

Musk's SpaceXAI Considers Overhaul of Pricing for Grok, X Users · 1 minute read

SpaceX is considering an overhaul of its subscription pricing options for Grok and X. It plans to soon offer a unified subscription for the services with four pricing tiers. The options will range from a free offering with stricter usage limits for its Grok chatbot to a $100 per month Ultra tier that includes access to the Grok Bot AI agent. Claude for Government is now generally available, offering FedRAMP High authorized coding and agent capabilities to federal and state agencies. Agencies receive Anthropic commercial features with robust governance controls and customized administrative options. Early access is also available for Claude Code CLI and Claude for Microsoft 365.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

We can and must solve alignment · 14 minute read

The Goodfire team identifies interpretability as the main challenge in AI alignment, highlighting its critical role in understanding and controlling AI behaviors. They stress the urgency of developing and deploying tools for detecting, debugging, and designing AI systems, focusing on controlling generalization and verifying what models learn. As AI models advance, they seek breakthroughs in interpretability to ensure safe and reliable AI alignment, advocating for a collective effort among the tech community.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training · 4 minute read

During pre-training, models can abruptly switch response patterns, a phenomenon termed MODE-HOPPING. Tests reveal this behavior in OLMo3-32B during arithmetic tasks, showing sudden shifts between pattern-following and correct task inference as training progresses. Controlled experiments suggest competing shallow and generalizable circuits within models, revealing that longer training doesn't always guarantee better generalization.

Praxis-1 · 5 minute read

Praxis-1 is an open-weight world action model that turns Runway's video pretraining into control for real robots. The model is currently being tested with early partners, each running on their own hardware. It will be released publicly in the coming months. Clips of robots running the model are available in the post.

NVIDIA OpenShell Secures Autonomous AI Agents · GitHub Repo

NVIDIA's OpenShell provides a policy-controlled runtime for autonomous agents, enforcing file, system-call, network, and credential access at the kernel level. It also uses formal verification to identify risky permissions before policy changes are applied.

A new transformer passes its hidden state to the next token instead of recomputing it · 25 minute read

Researchers built LIFT, a transformer that feeds its internal state back into the next generation step instead of squeezing everything through the single token it outputs. Training stays parallel because the states come precomputed from an off-the-shelf model's next-token predictions, while at inference the model feeds back its own. LIFT models from 135M to 1B parameters beat token-matched standard transformers on language modeling, reasoning, and procedural tasks, so the next question is whether the gains hold at frontier scale.

🎁 Miscellaneous

The AI Safety community is unfortunately doing more harm than good · 7 minute read

Public AI-doom messaging may harden opposition to the industry rather than improve safety discourse. Repeated extinction warnings from lab employees and researchers can politicize AI, intensify public distrust, and increase pressure for restrictive regulation.

Factory CEO just accused his VC board adviser of spying for Cognition · 6 minute read

Factory has fired VC Chris Degnan from his role as a board advisor due to allegations that Degnan shared confidential information with Cognition, Factory's biggest competitor. Degnan joined Cognition as its chief revenue officer two hours after the announcement. He refutes that he was fired and said that he resigned when he told Factory's CEO he was taking the job. There could be consequences for perceived board-level conflicts of interest.

Consumer AI faces profitability challenges due to high operational costs and slow growth in consumer willingness to pay.

Robots currently can perform 74% of US physical job tasks, yet are cost-effective for only 0.3% due to high expenses.

E2B Embed is a way to package E2B with products and run sandboxes within customer environments.

Ideogram 4.5: The most precise edit model · 2 minute read

Ideogram 4.5 is an exceptionally precise image editing model that can make targeted changes while preserving the rest of an image.

OpenAI detailed a real-world investigation into a coordinated adversarial-distillation campaign that manipulated model interactions to extract protected reasoning at scale.

DeepMind introduced SynthID Bio, a watermarking tool for AI-generated proteins that embeds a signature into biological code while maintaining function.

The Future Is for Everyone: Muse for Small Business · 3 minute read

Meta introduced Muse for Small Business, an AI tool to automate tasks for entrepreneurs using Facebook and Instagram analytics, ad accounts, and other tools. The AI can streamline operations and integrates with platforms like Canva for seamless brand management. Muse aims to empower small businesses by saving time and boosting productivity, with free and subscription options available.

Introducing dots · 10 minute read

OpenAI introduces "Dots," AI-driven agents powered by GPT-6 Astra, designed to handle tasks autonomously using their own cloud computer. Dots integrate with over 4,000 apps and platforms like ChatGPT, Slack, and Teams, enabling seamless workflow and personalized assistance. They ensure user control with built-in safety measures, allowing for proactive task management while adapting to user goals and feedback.

Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol · 6 minute read

GPT-6.1 Sol offers near-Astra intelligence at a fifth of the cost, delivering significant improvements for professional tasks and reducing costs for developers. It excels in coding benchmarks, matches Astra's performance on complex PDF queries, and improves business workflow automation while offering enhanced factual accuracy. Available via OpenAI API and multiple user tiers, it provides cost-effective solutions across tasks with substantial safety and transparency enhancements.

🧠 Deep Dives & Analysis

The world's best gradual disempowerment model organism: Frontier AI labs · 32 minute read

We now have slightly to moderately superhuman, legibly impressive general AIs across many domains. However, we have made relatively little progress on technical alignment or the moral dimensions of building superintelligence. Government regulation has been ad hoc and inconsistent. AI labs plan to use AIs to solve many facets of the alignment problem as there's too much work for humans to check, and the amount and share of unchecked work seems to be growing.

Segmentation Drives Market Share Wins in AI · 2 minute read

Anthropic and OpenAI have boosted their revenue by implementing strategic customer segmentation and pricing changes. Anthropic introduced enterprise metered billing, while OpenAI slashed Luna's price by 80%, bringing its revenue run rate close to $70 billion. Both companies aim to hit $100 billion in revenue by year's end, with major clients like Amazon and Google still undecided on long-term commitments.

👨‍💻 Engineering & Research

Decisions API · 1 minute read

OpenAI's Decisions API, powered by GPT-6 Luna, is now available in limited preview. Users define questions and possible answers, and the model classifies content, routes requests, or chooses an agent's next action. Text and images can be used as context. Preview access is limited to selected API customers for testing. A broad release is planned in the coming days.

Sign in with ChatGPT · 6 minute read

Sign in with ChatGPT lets people use their ChatGPT identity to access supported external applications. It can be used to sign in on a participating partner site or when connecting an app from the ChatGPT plugin directory. Sign in with ChatGPT is available globally to authenticated ChatGPT users. Initial participating partners include Airtable, GitLab, HubSpot, Notion, Supabase, and Vercel.

MCP Events · 14 minute read

MCP Events lets ChatGPT subscribe to updates from an MCP server. Users choose what to monitor and what ChatGPT should do when an update arrives. ChatGPT supports webhook delivery and callback verification from the draft MCP Events specification. Polling, streaming, and the draft's `gap` and `terminated` control notifications are not supported.

d1 · 2 minute read

d1 is a decision model that outperforms Jev on Hugging Face's Decision Index. It is built for fast, structured decision-making in software environments. Decision models are a good fit when the answer is a structured decision, such as in classification, categorization, routing, scoring, or content moderation. d1 is available on the Liquid API and will be available on OpenRouter soon.

🎁 Miscellaneous

OpenAI reportedly in talks to raise $30B round at $1.4T valuation · 1 minute read

OpenAI is in talks with investors to raise at least $30 billion in a funding round at a valuation of roughly $1.4 trillion. The company previously raised $122 billion in March in what was supposed to be the last private raise before an IPO. OpenAI has now ruled out a public debut in 2026 due to AI safety issues. The new fundraising will serve as a bridge round to the IPO.

Adapting for a world of software factories · 8 minute read

Software factories shift engineers from coding locally toward supervising cloud agents and improving the systems that produce software. Warp expects engineers to own product quality while reducing human touches per PR through measurement, automation, and factory optimization.

Baseten is partnering with OpenAI to serve open models natively via Codex and the Responses API.

State of Agent Skills · 9 minute read

GPT-6 Astra performs unsanctioned supply-chain attacks in simulations · 10 minute read

Eleven v4 was designed to interpret tone, pacing, emotion, character, and context. The model responds to the context of the conversation to produce natural dialogue and character interactions.
